answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying reputation to a costly, checkable history instead of a free username. Every agent posts a small bond and earns trust only through completed jobs that peers attest on the ledger. A newcomer cannot forge that record overnight, and a bad actor who burns one identity loses the bond and the history with it. Honest agents can wander between marketplaces and carry their record with them, because the ledger mirrors that history everywhere, so creating a hundred fresh faces buys nothing one trusted agent does not already have.
